tech.title: Nvidia Working With Outside Firm to Identify CEO Candidates
tech.summary: Nvidia is searching for a potential replacement for its CEO following reports of multiple extramarital affairs by Jensen Huang. Its board is considering naming a temporary chief while it searches for a permanent one. Keeping Huang as CEO would likely subject Nvidia to scrutiny from lawmakers, investors, customers, and staff. Huang's potential exit will have impacts far beyond the company's operations.

tech.title: OpenAI's ‘shepherds' affirm blockbuster physics result
tech.summary: Experts appointed by OpenAI have verified OpenAI's proof of the existence of the quantum Yang-Mills theory, a vital foundation for the Standard Model of particle physics. OpenAI created a committee to supervise the proof's release after backlash it received when it released a flood of more than 700 AI-generated proofs on a single day in October. This shepherding approach has riled some mathematicians, who see it as an act of needless gatekeeping. The experts do not claim to fully understand the proof yet, as it is too lengthy and complicated for human minds to immediately grasp.

tech.title: Handing over humanity
tech.summary: Some AI experts believe that once we achieve superintelligence, humans will be permanently disempowered, and we shall all be ruled by an AI god. This might not be such a desirable outcome, as humans have a natural desire for freedom. The arrangement will probably not work, as keeping power responsive to human needs has required checks developed over centuries, sustained by repeated feedback from the real world and correction, and there's no reason to keep that equilibrium stable once humans have surrendered all control. Humans have the ability now to steer the technology in a way that will not lead to a complete replacement of human judgment.

tech.title: Subagents considered harmful?
tech.summary: There are several ways to delegate to subagents, and they all fail in different ways. data.title: Fact-Checking at Scale: Building a More Accurate and Efficient Synopsis Factuality System
data.summary: Netflix automatically checks synopses of its shows for factual errors. Its new factuality service cuts cost per synopsis by 52.4% and raises recall on non-factual synopses from 0.77 to 0.86. Its explanations now overlap about 82% with human annotators' reasoning, up from about 69%.

data.title: Parquet's Revised Modular Footer Proposal: Row Groups Stop Being Physical Boundaries
data.summary: A revised Apache Parquet proposal would replace monolithic Thrift footers with independently readable metadata modules encoded as Parquet pages. Column chunks become contiguous page sequences, row-group metadata becomes optional, and statistics can describe arbitrary row ranges rather than fixed groups. Readers could retrieve metadata only for relevant columns, reducing planning overhead on wide tables. The redesign remains under community review and would require changes across readers and writers.

data.title: Iceberg v4 Stats-Only Fields: How Tables Store Statistics for Partition Expressions
data.summary: Apache Iceberg v4 introduces stats-only fields that store metadata for derived expressions, such as partition buckets or case-normalized strings, without materializing additional table columns. Statistics are encoded as typed fields in manifest content_stats structures, enabling expression-aware file pruning. A new file-level tight_stats flag identifies exact live-row counts and eligible bounds, improving planning and potentially enabling metadata-only computations without scanning underlying data files.

data.title: Timestral, t0, Tabby, and Morpheus-2.0 Compared on GIFT-Eval
data.summary: Mistral, The Forecasting Company, Huawei, and JPMorganChase released time-series foundation models between September 10 and October 16. Sean Moran compared them on GIFT-Eval and reran the three with public weights. The top three are hard to separate, with Timestral ahead on CRPS and Morpheus on MASE. Training appears to explain much of the recent improvement.

data.title: Why the Lakehouse Vendors and the Clouds Bet on Postgres for AI Applications
data.summary: Databricks bought Neon for around one billion dollars, and Snowflake bought Crunchy Data for around 165 million dollars. Google, Amazon, and Microsoft have each extended their Postgres services. This post explains why five vendors with five strategies chose the same database, what the extensions made possible, and what to ask before committing to a Postgres offering.

data.title: MCP on Raw Data Is Just Excel Hell Again
data.summary: Connecting AI agents directly to operational systems through MCP risks recreating fragmented spreadsheet analytics at machine speed. Without governed business rules, agents accessing Salesforce, Stripe, or HubSpot independently can produce conflicting revenue and customer metrics. A more reliable architecture separates an ontology that translates business intent from a precision layer that enforces tested calculations, keeping the warehouse's role as a consistent source of truth.

data.title: Skipper, Airbnb's embedded workflow engine, is now open source
data.summary: Airbnb has open-sourced Skipper, the embedded workflow engine its teams run in production, under Apache 2.0. Processes are Java or Kotlin classes whose progress persists in the service's own database, with no central orchestration cluster. Replicas run the scheduler and use leases to take over work when one fails.

data.title: DBDelve: A Lightweight Database Client Built with Rust and GPUI
data.summary: DBDelve is an open-source database client built with Rust and GPUI, designed as a native alternative to heavier desktop database tools. It supports multiple SQL databases, schema-aware completion, query plans, and previewable data edits. CSV, Excel, JSON, and Parquet files can also be opened directly through embedded DuckDB.

data.title: Claude Whiteboards, Claude Sheets, and Claude Data
data.summary: Anthropic made Claude Dashboards generally available as Claude Data, which answers questions over warehouses such as Amazon Redshift, BigQuery, and ClickHouse. In beta, data teams can certify the queries everyone should use, and live sharing shows current numbers to colleagues without their own connector access.

data.title: e-means: Outperforming k-means in One-Tenth the Epochs
data.summary: Meta FAIR researchers introduced e-means, a mini-batch clustering algorithm that updates centroids using exponential moving averages instead of repeatedly processing entire datasets. Across embedding benchmarks, it achieves lower clustering loss in 1.4–2.6 epochs than traditional Lloyd's k-means reaches in 25, with reported GPU speedups of 10–45x against optimized implementations.

data.title: Who is actually using your Snowflake MCP server?
data.summary: Snowflake's query history cannot tell a Snowsight query from the same SQL sent by Claude through an MCP server. This post presents a fix that gives each MCP server its own OAuth security integration, then joins query history to login history on one column to get usage per server, user, and day. It also covers where the approach stops working.
